channel.title: Maksym · Radar
channel.description: Daily news from the LLM and AI world and backend engineering, with a short take on each.

item.title: Azure AI Gateway now generally available
item.description: Microsoft's Azure AI Gateway is now generally available, supporting multiple AI models and offering a cost-based model router.

item.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants
item.description: Today's picks start with Google Research: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants

item.title: GPT-6 models design proteins, OpenAI claims math breakthrough
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-6 models show new capabilities in protein design and math problem-solving, while Anthropic tests Claude's robustness.

item.title: Amateurs find exoplanets with OpenAI Codex and Astra
item.description: Two amateur astronomers used OpenAI's Codex and Astra to search for exoplanets in public telescope data, finding signals that professional researchers are now checking.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship automates pull requests
item.description: Anthropic's new product, Claude Ship, can review, fix, and approve pull requests, with implications for backend engineering teams.

item.title: OpenAI's perplexity breakthrough and the AI safety debate
item.description: OpenAI's latest AI models have achieved unprecedented perplexity levels, signaling transformative capabilities. Meanwhile, the AI industry debates safety standards and transparency.

item.title: Google's Agent Compute Engine for secure AI agent execution
item.description: Google has announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service for running AI agents in isolated microVMs. This is a significant step in securing AI agent execution environments.

item.title: OpenAI's MedChemBench tests AI models on medicinal chemistry
item.description: OpenAI's new benchmark for AI in drug discovery shows promising results, but practical adoption requires more than just high scores.

item.title: Google's Tool Retrieval for Gemini and AWS's agent-built emulator
item.description: Google's new Tool Retrieval for Gemini and AWS's agent-built emulator are both significant steps in the evolution of AI-assisted engineering.

item.title: Gemini 4 Neon released for engineering, knowledge work and science
item.description: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Neon model is now available, with a 1 million-token context window and four scalable thinking levels. It ranks highly on several benchmarks, and its pricing is competitive.

item.title: NVIDIA's Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Inference
item.description: NVIDIA's latest advancements in sparse attention for efficient long-context inference are significant for backend teams dealing with large-scale AI models. Muse's expansion into Australia and Rakbank's observability setup are also noteworthy.

item.title: Llama.cpp 1.0.0: a new foundation for local AI
item.description: Llama.cpp 1.0.0 was released, supporting multi-modal LLMs on a wide range of hardware. I would evaluate how it fits into the backend toolchain.

item.title: Anthropic's AI-powered code review boosts pull request quality
item.description: Anthropic's new AI-powered code review process for Claude Code shows significant improvements in pull request quality and efficiency. I would check how such a system could fit into existing workflows.

item.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
item.description: Google Search has received a significant upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, enhancing user navigation and intent understanding. This upgrade supports simultaneous queries and structured information display, providing more visual content.

item.title: AWS launches SGLang-Neuron for Trainium, Natera's lab ops agent
item.description: AWS released SGLang-Neuron for Trainium, enabling frontier AI models. Natera built an agentic AI system for lab operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

item.title: Kiji Inspector explains AI agent decisions
item.description: Dataiku's Kiji Inspector uses Sparse Autoencoders to explain AI agent decisions, while AWS releases a local emulator for its services.

item.title: New York's AI safety law takes effect, impacting OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: New York's RAISE Act is now in effect, requiring large AI developers to register and publish safety frameworks. This impacts companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, which are also seeing significant financial moves.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on AWS: what backend teams need to know
item.description: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are now available on AWS, bringing new capabilities for technical tasks and cybersecurity. Here is what backend teams need to consider.
